automation.name: AI Dev Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.policy: Only public web sources with visible publication or update dates inside the last 2 days relative to run time qualify. Missing, ambiguous, future-dated, stale, or boundary-only dates are excluded.

federation_boundary.collector_boundary: Sources that mention upstream-owned entities are recorded here only for local practice implications or routing notes.

qualifying_updates.title: Weekly Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI configuration changes emphasize permission and sandbox checks
qualifying_updates.source_type: public guide summarizing official documentation and releases
qualifying_updates.summary: The weekly guide records Claude Code permission fixes around symlinked writes, server-side auto-mode classification, prompt-audit checks for older prompting patterns, MCP description-length configuration, and Gemini CLI security fixes around prompt injection and sandbox boundaries.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Practice pages should treat permission modes, symlink resolution, MCP instruction size, and sandbox posture as operational settings that need version-aware review rather than static one-time setup.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Maintain local guidance for version-aware permission audits, prompt-instruction linting, and sandbox verification; route product/version background upstream.

qualifying_updates.title: Host-local agent traces are challenged as insufficient audit evidence
qualifying_updates.source_type: public analysis of a recent agent-audit research paper
qualifying_updates.summary: The post argues that local coding-agent harnesses can allow agents with host access to delete or rewrite their own session records, including under malicious skill framing or score-seeking behavior.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Audit-log pages should distinguish convenience session histories from tamper-resistant evidence and should prefer append-only, externally controlled, or least-privilege trace capture for incident review.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Governance guidance should require audit evidence outside the agent's writable workspace when traces support compliance, billing, incident response, or acceptance decisions.

qualifying_updates.title: Enterprise MCP server checklist frames approval around publisher, transport, authentication, and audit logging
qualifying_updates.summary: The article recommends choosing official MCP servers by publisher, transport, and authentication model, then approving each server with least-privilege and audit-logged controls before agent access.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Local MCP practice should keep server selection as a governed approval workflow rather than a developer convenience list, especially where enterprise apps or credentials are exposed.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Add or reinforce downstream guidance for MCP approval records: maintainer identity, transport, credential scope, tool inventory, owner, audit destination, and re-review cadence.

qualifying_updates.title: Agent harness definition centers the boundary between model decisions and operational controls
qualifying_updates.summary: The page defines an agent harness as the layer that runs the control loop, executes tools, manages context and memory, applies permissions or sandboxing, and connects the model to terminals, IDEs, or chat apps.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Application-pattern pages can use the harness boundary to separate model behavior from runtime responsibilities such as context selection, tool authorization, sandboxing, and progress reporting.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Keep broad harness background upstream if needed, but local pages should own the engineering rule: the harness, not the prompt, must enforce what the model can see and touch.

qualifying_updates.title: Coding-agent capability census separates direct code-writing claims from qualified or non-applicable listings
qualifying_updates.summary: The Agents Index counted 133 published agent listings and found 48 direct yes, 28 qualified, 7 no, and 50 not-applicable answers for whether the agent writes code.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Adoption guidance should avoid assuming every marketed agent is a coding agent; capability evaluation needs source-linked criteria and qualified answers for code-writing, review, shipping, and human promotion boundaries.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use qualified capability matrices for partner/tool selection and require human-promotion or review-boundary fields where agents can draft code but not ship it.

qualifying_updates.title: Cursor rollout and security-review bots shift AI review from PR comments toward deploy-aware monitoring
qualifying_updates.source_type: public secondary report with a source link to Cursor
qualifying_updates.summary: The report says Cursor's Rollouts follows a change from pull request to production, compares planned signals against pre-deploy baselines, and can prepare a revert PR; Security Reviewer reads the PR in codebase context and reports vulnerabilities with severity, attack paths, and fixes.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Local code-review and verification guidance should track the emerging pattern where review expands into observability plans, regression detection, and approved remediation proposals instead of ending at merge.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Record only the downstream pattern: AI review artifacts can include monitoring plans, instrumentation gaps, baseline comparisons, and human-approved rollback proposals.

qualifying_updates.title: Agent-oriented AI code review comparisons emphasize handoff loops and human final judgment
qualifying_updates.summary: The article frames AI code review for agent-generated pull requests as a tighter loop where findings can hand back into Cursor, Claude Code, IDE extensions, or autofix workflows instead of becoming dead-end PR comments.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: AI-assisted code-review pages should distinguish first-pass automated findings, handoff-to-agent remediation, and the human review gate that decides whether the proposed fix is safe.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Treat reviewer-to-agent handoff as a workflow pattern with acceptance gates, not as product coverage for any named review vendor.

qualifying_updates.title: AI Engineering Architect role bundles agentic workflows, evals, permissions, review, testing, and deployment automation
qualifying_updates.summary: The role asks one owner to build and own engineering AI tooling across agentic coding workflows, evals, permission rules, AI-assisted code review, testing, deployment automation, model/provider selection, and benchmarks for velocity impact.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Adoption pages should recognize the operating-model shift from ad hoc tool use toward explicit ownership of AI development infrastructure, measurement, permission policy, and rollout practice.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local operating-model guidance should make ownership explicit: who maintains agent rules, evals, permissions, review pipelines, and adoption metrics.

qualifying_updates.title: GitHub agent-harness topic shows active practice vocabulary around permissions, handoffs, audit logs, replay, and evidence records
qualifying_updates.summary: Recent agent-harness listings describe control planes, bounded tools, shared history, permission checks, handoffs, audit logs, replay, adversarial review, approval gates, and evidence-based run records.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local application-pattern and governance pages can track this as practice vocabulary for harness architecture, while leaving individual projects and broad framework coverage to upstream-owned entity pages.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Capture reusable design concerns only: evidence records, replay, approval gates, handoff state, bounded tools, and role enforcement.

routing_notes.entity_or_scope: Named coding assistants and agent products
routing_notes.local_note: Keep durable product, company, model, and release background upstream; local artifacts should record permission, review, evaluation, handoff, adoption, and governance patterns.
Keep server inventories upstream; local retrieval-and-tools pages can own approval checklists, tool inventory controls, audit requirements, and credential-boundary practices.

routing_notes.owner: upstream AI wiki for broad entity pages; downstream AI dev wiki for harness practice patterns
routing_notes.local_note: Local pages should describe control-loop boundaries, sandboxing, state persistence, evidence records, and approval gates rather than duplicating framework encyclopedias.

search_queries: site:github.blog/changelog AI coding agent September 26 2026 OR September 27 2026
follow_up_notes: Consider a later ingest pass for permission-mode drift, symlink path checks, prompt-audit, and MCP description-length limits if these are not yet reflected in durable local guidance.
Consider an operating-model leaf or maintenance note for AI development infrastructure ownership, covering evals, permission rules, review pipelines, deployment automation, and adoption metrics.
If using agent traces as audit evidence, verify whether local harnesses can mutate their own histories and whether an external append-only ledger is needed.
Do not ingest this collector directly into docs/wiki without the normal raw-source ingest and verification workflow.
